planting.note: Plant dormant divisions or potted plants in fall so roots establish before winter bloom.

directions: Amethyst Gem produces rounded, double to semi-double flowers in rich amethyst-purple tones that deepen with age and contrast against glossy, leathery evergreen foliage. Nodding blooms open in late winter to early spring on sturdy stems held above the clump. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled shade beneath deciduous trees, where it tolerates dry shade once established. Remove tattered old leaves in late winter just as flower buds emerge to showcase the blooms.

planting.note: Fall planting lets the clump settle before its first winter bloom cycle.

directions: Blue Diamond carries slate-blue to smoky violet double flowers held just above mounded, dark evergreen leaves, a cooler-toned counterpart to the more common pink and plum hybridus seedlings. Flowering runs from late winter into early spring and persists for several weeks as the sepals age to green. Best sited in humus-rich soil under high deciduous shade where summer moisture is consistent but winter drainage is sharp. Established clumps are long-lived and resent disturbance, so divide only when vigor declines.

planting.note: Install in fall so plants root in before the earliest late-winter buds appear.

directions: Red Sapphire bears deep wine-red, outward-facing cupped flowers with a satiny sheen that catches low winter light against a backbone of sturdy, deeply lobed evergreen leaves. Bloom begins in late winter and overlaps with early spring bulbs, making it a strong companion for shade borders. It performs best in cool, evenly moist, well-drained woodland soil and declines in hot, waterlogged sites. Mulch lightly with leaf litter each fall to mimic its native forest-floor conditions.

planting.note: Fall transplanting gives roots a full season before flowering begins.

directions: Double Slate opens fully double, many-petaled flowers in smoky slate-gray and dusky plum tones that shift subtly as the bloom ages on the plant. The sturdy flower stalks rise above a clump of glossy, palmate evergreen foliage from late winter into spring. It thrives in part shade with rich, humus-laden soil and benefits from consistent moisture during its fall-to-spring growing season. Cut back winter-worn old leaves before new flower stems emerge to keep the display clean.

planting.note: Plant in fall; blooms arrive the following late winter once roots are established.

directions: Painted Singles produces single, saucer-shaped flowers heavily splashed and veined in contrasting color over a lighter base, giving each bloom a hand-brushed, watercolor look. Flowering runs from late winter through early spring on a compact clump of leathery, evergreen leaves. Grow in part to full shade in fertile, well-drained soil that stays cool and moist in summer. Being a single-flowered seed-strain selection, seedlings may show some variation, but the painted picotee patterning is a consistent hallmark.

planting.note: Fall planting suits this evergreen perennial's late-winter bloom cycle.

directions: This anemone-form selection from the Winter Delights strain carries outer sepals surrounding a dense, frilled ring of small nectary petals, giving each flower extra depth and texture compared to plain single blooms. Color ranges across soft blush, cream, and dusky rose depending on the individual plant. It flowers from late winter into early spring above a mound of leathery, dark green evergreen leaves. Site in humus-rich, well-drained part shade and avoid summer waterlogging.

scientific_name: Helleborus x hybridus 'Winter Delights Double Bicolor'

planting.note: Fall planting establishes roots ahead of the first late-winter flowering.

directions: Winter Delights Double Bicolor produces fully double flowers with a contrasting two-tone pattern, typically a darker picotee edge over a paler center, layered in rounded petaloid sepals. Blooms nod on strong stems above a tidy clump of glossy, dark evergreen foliage from late winter through early spring. It prefers part to full shade and rich, well-drained soil that does not dry out completely in summer. As a seed-strain selection, individual plants vary somewhat in exact color balance while retaining the bicolor double form.

planting.note: Fall planting lets this short-lived species settle before its winter growth flush.

directions: Krenitsky is a selection of the species Helleborus foetidus grown for its finely divided, blue-gray-green foliage that is narrower and more feathery than typical seedlings. Clusters of small, bell-shaped chartreuse flowers edged in maroon appear on branched stems from late winter into spring, held above the evergreen leaf rosette. It self-sows readily where happy and is best treated as a short-lived perennial that renews itself from seedlings. Give it sharply drained, lean soil in light to moderate shade, since rich, wet ground shortens its life.

scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'Ice N' Roses Barolo'

planting.note: Plant this patented interspecific hellebore in fall ahead of its winter bloom season.

directions: Ice N' Roses Barolo is a selection from the Ice N' Roses series of Helleborus x glandorfensis, named for its deep, wine-dark burgundy-red outward-facing flowers reminiscent of the Italian red wine. Blooms appear early, often beginning in midwinter, over a compact mound of glossy, evergreen, leathery foliage. This vegetatively propagated series was bred for uniform, floriferous garden performance compared with seed-grown x hybridus strains. Grow in part shade with rich, well-drained soil and consistent moisture for the longest bloom display.

scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'Ice N' Roses Bianco'

planting.note: Fall planting establishes this clonal selection before its early winter flowering.

directions: Ice N' Roses Bianco is a white-flowered selection in the Ice N' Roses series of Helleborus x glandorfensis, bearing clean, pure white, outward-facing blooms that brighten a winter shade garden before most perennials stir. Flowers appear over evergreen, glossy, leathery foliage and often begin as early as midwinter in milder climates. As a vegetatively propagated clone, it offers consistent flower form and bloom timing year to year. Plant in part shade with humus-rich, well-drained soil and avoid letting it sit in standing winter water.

scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'Ice N' Roses Merlot'

planting.note: Install this clone in fall for roots to settle before midwinter bloom.

directions: Ice N' Roses Merlot bears dark, purple-tinged red flowers, deeper and more wine-toned than its sibling Barolo, over a tidy clump of glossy evergreen leaves. It is a selection in the Ice N' Roses series of Helleborus x glandorfensis, bred for early, reliable midwinter flowering and compact habit. The outward-facing blooms hold their color well as they age, extending the display into early spring. Grow in part shade with rich, well-drained soil, and mulch lightly to protect the crown through hard freezes.

scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'Ice N' Roses Picotee'

planting.note: Fall planting gives this clonal selection a full season to establish before bloom.

directions: Ice N' Roses Picotee shows white, outward-facing flowers finely edged in a thin rose-pink picotee margin, a crisper and more compact counterpart to seed-strain picotee hybridus types. It is a vegetatively propagated selection in the Ice N' Roses series of Helleborus x glandorfensis, flowering as early as midwinter over glossy evergreen foliage. The clean picotee edging intensifies slightly as flowers age in cold weather. Grow in part shade with well-drained, humus-rich soil, keeping the crown from sitting in winter wet.

scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'Ice N' Roses Rosado'

planting.note: Plant in fall so this clone roots in before its early winter bloom.

directions: Ice N' Roses Rosado, whose Spanish name means rose-pink, produces clear rosy-pink, outward-facing flowers over a compact dome of glossy, leathery evergreen leaves. Part of the Ice N' Roses series of Helleborus x glandorfensis, it was bred for early, uniform midwinter flowering well before most perennials break dormancy. Its vegetative propagation ensures consistent color and habit from plant to plant, unlike variable seed-grown strains. Grow in part shade in rich, well-drained soil, and protect young plants with mulch through their first winter.
